# 2 Baruch Chapter 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 4:2 — "the true one" — parenthetical identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "this-is-[only] that-which-shall-be-revealed" | Brackets implied contrast; "only" added |
| LOGOS | "it is that which shall be revealed with me" | Formal, no addition |
| PNEUMA | "The real one is in my keeping" | Paraphrase — "real" and "in my keeping" both interpretive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "That which shall be revealed with me" preserves the eschatological disclosure language. EMET's "only" is an over-addition; PNEUMA's "real" and "in my keeping" are functional but lose the revelation vocabulary.

---

## 4:5 — "likeness of the tabernacle and all its vessels"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-likeness-of-the-tabernacle and-all-its-vessels" | Literal compound |
| LOGOS | "the likeness of the tabernacle and all its vessels" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the pattern of the tabernacle and all its furnishings" | "Pattern" (Exod 25:9 LXX); "furnishings" for "vessels" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Likeness" for the Syriac preserves the visionary/heavenly template sense. "Vessels" preferred over "furnishings" — the Syriac here likely refers to sacred utensils specifically, not general furniture.

---

## 4:6 — "my Anointed One" vs. "my Messiah"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "my-Anointed-One" | Literal compound of the Syriac meshiha |
| LOGOS | "my Anointed One" | Formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "my Messiah" | Transliteration familiar to modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "My Anointed One" retains the semantic content; "Messiah" as transliteration is better suited to Christian theological commentary than translation. The Syriac title should be rendered, not transliterated.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
